rationale: PINS the `exports` relationship type on kotlin (DERIV_EXPORTS_KOT3). Kotlin has NO export statement: probe A over a 600-file corpus walk counted 233 distinct grammar node types and none of export_declaration / export_list / export_statement among them (validation/m14/results/kotlin-ontology-census.txt). What kotlin DOES define is that a top-level declaration is `public` unless it says otherwise, while `internal` restricts to the module and `private` to the file. So the compilation unit's published surface is exactly { top-level declaration whose visibility is `public` or absent }, and that is what these expectations assert. Probe B8 measured 4,180 such declarations across 558 of 600 files, so this is the majority case and not a corner. The publication's source is the file's first top-level TYPE (PublicType here); a file with no top-level type publishes no relationship and reports metadata.exportsWithheldNoModuleIdentity instead. The SCOPE cases are here because omitting getter/setter/lambda_literal from extractProperty's scope scan (real-kotlin-analyzer.ts:1548) published locals as part of the exported surface — 24 analyzer-only edges over a 120-file draw, 22 of them a val inside a block-valued get(). The expectations below were authored from the kotlin language rule and re-probed; script/m60/kotlin-exports-oracle.ts is the independent walker that measures agreement at 100.0% over 200 files (417 truth edges, 0 missing, 0 extra).

expectRelationships.note: basis pin: a declaration with NO visibility modifier is published by the FILE as default-public; the pre-fix field logic claimed explicit-public for everything, so a mutant that always says explicit-public must fail HERE (metadata.via is the current field spelling).

forbidRelationships.comment: internal restricts a top-level declaration to the MODULE, so it is not part of the consumer surface
private restricts a top-level declaration to the FILE
a member of PublicType is reachable through PublicType, not published under its own name
a member of WithAccessor, not a top-level declaration
a member of WithLambda, not a top-level declaration
a member of WithLambda, not a top-level declaration
a member of PublishedObject, reachable through the object

a val inside a block-valued get() is a LOCAL. The pinned grammar puts it at statements < function_body < getter < class_body, with no function_declaration on the chain, so the pre-fix scope scan walked past the accessor and published it. This forbid is the regression pin for that defect.
a val inside a lambda assigned to a class property is a LOCAL. The chain is ... < lambda_literal < property_declaration < class_body, again with no function_declaration. Second regression pin.
a val inside a method body is a local; the pre-fix scan already stopped at function_declaration and this forbid guards that branch

forbidSymbols.name: insideGetter
forbidSymbols.comment: local inside a property accessor — must not become a symbol at all

forbidSymbols.name: insideLambda
forbidSymbols.comment: local inside a lambda literal — must not become a symbol at all

forbidSymbols.name: insideMethod
forbidSymbols.comment: local inside a method body — must not become a symbol at all

expectNoRelationshipWhereSourceIsPath.comment: the module identity is the file's first top-level TYPE. An earlier version fell back to the FILE PATH when a file declared no type, which put a 90-character absolute path in the source of every edge; 24 of 26 analyzer-only edges over a 120-file draw were exactly that. parallel-indexer.ts:3451 drops an export edge whose source cannot resolve to a symbol, so those rows were unreadable as well as unmatchable.

expectMetadataAbsenceWhy: this file DOES declare a top-level type (PublicType), so no name is withheld for want of a module identity and the field is ABSENT rather than 0 — a zero is a claim that the count was measured to be zero, an absent field is an unknown. The no-module-identity branch is pinned separately by kotlin/exports-no-module-identity, which expects 3.

expectPublicationBasis.comment: publicationBasis names WHICH rule published the declaration, and it must be able to report both arms. The first version read `s.visibility === 'public'`, which is always true because determineVisibility returns the literal 'public' for a declaration that said nothing, so every edge claimed explicit-public and the default-public arm was dead code — while 1,334 of 4,180 published declarations in the 600-file walk said nothing. Kotlin's default-public convention is the MAJORITY case and was being reported as the minority one.

evidence.oracleAgreement: 100.0% (417/417 truth edges, 0 oracle-only, 0 analyzer-only) at KOT_ORACLE_N=200
